candidates.snippet: Daoism (also romanized as Taoism) generally names one of the three main currents of traditional Chinese thought, although it should be obvious that like any "ism," it is an abstraction—what it names is not a uniform but multifaceted tradition with rich internal differences. Specifically, "Daoism" encompasses both a philosophical tradition and an organized religion, which in modern Chinese are identified separately as daojia and daojiao , respectively. The two are deeply intertwined, and Laozi (or Lao-tzu) figures centrally in both. Philosophical Daoism traces its origins to Laozi, an extraordinary thinker who flourished during the sixth century B.C.E., according to Chinese sources. According to some modern scholars, however, Laozi is entirely legendary; there was never a historical Laozi. In religious Daoism, Laozi is revered as a supreme deity.
